body: **2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — (the MCP wait cap, a driver-only bound) §8 Timeout extensions: the MCP `wait` tool clamps `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, which is also its default (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`). The bound falls on the driver only: the plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving session, never a person. Why it matters: this is the precedent this chunk extends. That chunk closed `wait` "below the client's tool-call timeout" without a measured client bound. This chunk measures that bound and must keep `contract/mcp-wait-tool/timeout-ms` and the driver-only framing true for every tool it caps.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — §8: a verified `send` waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s), then is refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed. A human key during the wait takes the wheel and the send is refused `human-typing`; the outer-PTY case `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` is sequenced on the wrapper's lines, never a timer. Why it matters: the gate is one segment of `send`'s longest block. Any cap or split must leave `contract/send-refusal/input-not-ready`, `decision/human-key-takes-the-wheel` and "the human always wins" unchanged.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — §8: once typed, a confirmed `send` waits within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), or within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL) for `/compact` on a verified CLI. If it is not confirmed in time the result is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`, a bound on the driver only. Why it matters: the 40 s compact window plus the 8.5 s gate is `send`'s longest block. The chunk must sum these against the client's tool-call timeout. Any change touches `contract/send-refusal/no-prompt-submitted` and the time-bound rows.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** — §8 Timeout extensions changed from "no limit on a human" to a dialog deadline that bounds the driver's `answer` path only; on expiry the dialog renders for the human. Why it matters: this is the origin of the rule that every viola time bound falls on the driver, never the human. A new MCP call bound must keep that rule.

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — the dialog hold became `dialog_hold_s`, 60–3600 s, default 60, under a `hooks.json` timeout of 3615 s and a hook bound of 3605 s. At the end of the hold the wrapper appends `dialog-expired`, which wakes `wait`; any human key hands the dialog back. Why it matters: the hold can reach 3600 s and wakes a parked `wait`, so it bears on whether the MCP `answer`/`wait` blocks stay under the client bound (`contract/config-json/dialog-hold-s`, `contract/event-line/dialog-expired`, `decision/dialog-hold-bounds-the-driver`).

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — (the dialog hold bounds owned by 0.2.0's first entry) `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` / `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` stay PROVISIONAL, owned by 0.2.0's first entry. Why it matters: these are bound constants this chunk may meet while listing every tool's longest block. Their PROVISIONAL marks and owner must be kept.

**2026-11-15-live-round-on-the-trimmed-product** — `~ decision/dialog-hold-bounds-the-driver`: state moved from provisional to standing after the hold's ceiling was measured live. Why it matters: this picked row now stands. A bound this chunk adds over `answer` must not contradict it.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` and `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` dropped the budget pause from the list of bounds; `~ contract/cli-exit-codes/11` is retired and never reused (an older wrapper's `budget-paused` reads `unknown`, 14). Why it matters: these are the two rows that enumerate every time bound viola holds. A new MCP call bound or cap extends that list. The retired exit 11 must not be reused for a timeout refusal.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` dropped the 5 s status-line deadline. Why it matters: this is the second precedent for editing the enumerated time-bound rows when a bound comes or goes. This chunk follows the same form if it adds an MCP tool-call bound.

**2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola** — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` gained "the start's Claude config lock wait", falling on viola's own start. `~ decision/run-diagnostics-off-terminal` gained the trust step's single `trust-record` diagnostics line, never a refusal, exit code or hint. Why it matters: this is the latest form of the two time-bound rows this chunk would extend. It also sets the precedent that a new kind of bound-bearer is named in the rule itself.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — §8: `list` and `revive` each make one `claude agents --json` read, with a 5 s kill and `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`. A failed or timed-out read fails open, and the bound falls on viola's own child. Why it matters: the MCP `list` tool's longest block includes this read (`decision/claude-agents-read-fails-open`). It must be counted against the client's tool-call timeout.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** — (the plugin against an impostor wrapper) a new not-assertable entity: an MCP frame tool (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`) meeting a server that is not the recorded wrapper returns `isError` `instance-unreachable` with no frame (`server_verified` in `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`). Why it matters: the server check is part of `send`'s client-side checks, which this chunk must bound. Under `decision/no-assertions-for-plugin-and-ipc`, MCP results write no human-facing byte.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — (the plugin against a strict-modes-refused instance) a new not-assertable entity: MCP frame tools run the instance check in `frame` before `live_endpoint` and return `isError` `instance-unreachable` with no frame and no line. Why it matters: this is another client-side step on each MCP tool's path. It also sets the precedent that MCP refusals stay out of a11y assertions.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — (MCP's `isError` body names its cause; a lost wrapper reads `endpoint-lost`) MCP's `isError` body is the CLI's document without `v`, with `detail` `server-verify-failed` / `strict-modes-failed`. A wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`. Exit 21's closed causes are listed. Why it matters: a call cut at a bound must map to an existing closed word or a new one shown at P4. The cause set (`contract/instance-unreachable-detail/*`, `contract/instance-unreachable-json/document`) and the rule against shared hints (`decision/one-hint-per-code`, `decision/no-hint-names-release`) bind any new code.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — (peer refusal screened to a code word; a fault's body; the census of error writers; `--json`'s exit-2 exception) A peer's non-code-word refusal reads `unknown`, and a non-code-word detail reads nothing (null on MCP). A fault outside the five known reads `wrapper fault`. Each error body needs a writer and a witness, and `thiserror` messages interpolate nothing. The `send`/`answer` exit-2 paths write a fixed line and no document. Why it matters: a timeout result or error class this chunk adds on MCP or the CLI must pass these rows (`decision/peer-replies-screened-to-code-words`, `decision/error-bodies-have-writer-and-witness`, `decision/thiserror-messages-interpolate-nothing`, `contract/fault-body/message`, `contract/cli-json-failure/send-answer-exit-2`).

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** — (hook and MCP on a refused socket directory; the client euid refusal's limit of proof) MCP frame tools return `isError` `instance-unreachable` / `socket-dir-refused` past the live endpoint, with no frame and no line. The client euid decision is tested over injected euids, and seam wiring is read only in remove-the-guard runs. Why it matters: these are more client-side steps on the MCP path to bound (`contract/mcp-frame-tool/socket-dir-refused`). The euid limit of proof (`decision/client-euid-refusal-test-strategy`) sets how far a test of the shared connect can go.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — (the a11y cases' CI home; the server-verify and socket-directory carve-outs retired) The cli/tui cases run in the `test` job's `coverage` suite on `ubuntu-latest` alone, with `gate --require coverage,doctest` as the verdict. The server-identity and socket-dir witnesses run ungated there. Why it matters: any test this chunk adds that "can fail" runs on that one leg with zero retries (`decision/zero-flakiness`).

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — (the §8 verification lines pinned by literal; cli checks on std::process::Command) Every fixed CLI string, hints included, is pinned by literal. The typed exit codes and a hint-free `--json` are asserted over `std::process::Command`. Why it matters: a new or changed refusal, hint or result line from a capped argument or a split takes a literal pin (`decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned`, `decision/refusal-layout-literal-pins`).

**2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal** — `~ contract/viola-verify/step-line`: changed from `pass|fail` to `pass|absent|fail`, with `absent` only on the browser-tools-prompt row. Why it matters: if the bound becomes a relied ledger row with a `viola verify` probe (a 30th row), it prints a new `[NN/NN]` step line. That line must fit this contract, and `NN/NN` moves.

**2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically** — `~ contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes`, `~ contract/tui-passthrough/viola-terminal-bytes` and `~ decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked`: a start's automatic verify window, before the child exists, is the one exception. Keys typed then wait in the terminal's buffer, and verify's lines L1–L5 and its output precede the child's bytes. Why it matters: a 30th verify row with a probe lengthens that window and its output. This is a PROVISIONAL exception that the chunk's ledger-row fork would widen.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — a `verify` stopped by Ctrl-C/TERM before its rows are checked prints no step line and no summary, only the `unable:` / `hint:` pair, and exits 1. The stop path adds no time bound. Why it matters: a new verify probe must keep the interrupted pair and add no bound on the stop path (`contract/interrupted-verify/*`, `contract/viola-verify/interrupted-pair`).

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — (the tui boundary after a contained vt100 feed panic) after the panic, the driver's `send` is refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` (exit 13) while a human key still reaches the child, and no viola literal reaches the outer terminal. Why it matters: this is one of `send`'s refusal paths on the bounded path. Any change to `send`'s waits must keep `contract/tui-passthrough/after-feed-panic`.

**2026-11-20-a-quoted-modal-never-blocks-a-send** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing`: the readiness predicate also reads the compiled shapes over the compiled literals. Why it matters: `send`'s readiness read, part of its longest block, parses the vendor screen only within this row. A bound or split must not widen what is parsed.

**2026-11-19-context-as-a-local-command** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing` except: the test-only rig reads box-row cell attributes after a turn end or send, as closed words, never text (two keys: x, DEL). Why it matters: this is the rig reading behind the carry `cry-ujze4atl` (`rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del`). If that red is met in this chunk, the mend must stay inside this exception, with no retry (`decision/zero-flakiness`).

**2026-11-12T03-23-49-rows** — every area of the master became rows, each verified against the code. Relied rows are kept or cut, and guards are re-pointed. Why it matters: this is the form every picked row takes. Any edit this chunk proposes is a `+`/`~`/`−` on a row with its reason, as the later entries show.

Bounds every tool the viola MCP server serves (send, wait, last, answer, list) in code, each tool's longest block sitting below the claude CLI MCP client's tool-call timeout.
Establishes that client timeout for the versions viola stamps as a reading from the installed bundles' strings: its default, the names that move it, stdio difference, progress-notification reset, and what the client does at the bound.
Covers send's whole path (client-side checks, the frame, the wrapper's wheel read, typing and delivery confirmation) and wait's caller-supplied wait.
Where a tool's block can exceed the client's bound today, closes the gap by a compiled bound, a cap on a caller's argument, or a documented split, with a test that can fail.
How the bound stands (a relied capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe, or a compiled bound with a test and a drift reading) is a fork left to P3.

body: The MCP server's tools and their deadlines: every tool's longest block bounded in code and below the MCP client's tool-call timeout.
The MCP wait tool's caller-supplied timeout_ms: capped, or otherwise held, so the caller's wait cannot carry the call past the client's bound.

Send's confirmation and its waits: the wrapper's wheel read, typing and delivery confirmation that the send tool shares with the CLI send path through the channel's Tokio client, all inside the tool's bound.

Send refused while the human types, and the send refusals input-not-ready and no-prompt-submitted: a bound on send's path ends in these refusals, never in waiting on or blocking the human's keystrokes.
Time bounds fall on the driver only and never on the human: every bound this chunk adds or tightens is the driver's (the MCP caller's), with no time limit put on the person at the terminal.
Dialog hold bounds the driver, and config.json dialog_hold_s: the answer tool's and wait tool's blocks around a pending dialog must stay below the client's bound alongside the dialog hold.

The MCP server frame tools' refusals (socket-dir-refused, strict-modes-failed, server-verify-failed) and the socket-directory and strict-modes refusals coming before any frame or write: the client-side checks on send's path stay first and inside the bound.

The fault body under --json and on MCP: a tool reaching its bound returns a fault or refusal body with its code word, faults carrying no hint, thiserror messages interpolating nothing, peer replies screened to code words.
Code word format, one hint per code, no hint naming a release, and the unknown refusal carrying no hint: any new code word a bound's expiry adds follows these.

The CLI wait and send path the MCP tools share: viola wait's waiting line and timed_out outcome, and the CLI exit codes for an unreachable instance, keep their form where the shared client's bounds change.
The wrapper's send handling under run: zero viola bytes on the terminal and run diagnostics never reaching it, so a bound or deadline added there writes nothing to the TUI passthrough.
Live readings never gate: the client timeout is read from the installed bundles' strings with no live start, a reading and not a measurement, and no test depends on a live claude.

If the bound becomes a relied ledger row, viola verify's step line and its interrupted pair stay in form for the new probe; whatever verify newly reads, writes or spawns reaches no file, stamp, fixture or log as text.
Fixed CLI strings pinned by literal and fixed copy from design: any new refusal, fault or code word text the bound adds is pinned by a literal test.

Zero flakiness with no retries: the open intermittent rig rehearsal red is mended only after its cause is read, with no retry rule and no loosened wait, and each new bound's test can fail deterministically.

body_fields.convention: a11y assertions run inside the existing test suites, as nextest failures, with no a11y suite or driver of their own
the CI test gate allows no skips, requires coverage and doctest, and a gate breach fails the build
tests flake never and are never retried, and the mutation audit covers the invariants held in crate tests
every fixed CLI or tool string a test pins is pinned by its literal
boundary tests are sequenced on records and never inspect claude's own content

body: Colour and SGR rules (bold names, amber dialog word, dim stale rows, colour decision inputs, name truncation): the chunk adds no styled output.
Screen-reader targets and setups and the manual Orca and keyboard passes: the chunk changes no read-aloud surface and runs no manual pass.
viola revive and its --json refusals, revive --list, and start-against-holder refusals: the chunk touches no start or revive path.
viola link and unlink, plugin install, and viola --help output: none of these surfaces is reached by a tool's bound.

Absences of internationalization, a touch surface, a web or graphical frontend or a rendered page, and the not-applicable harness areas (contrast, focus management, WCAG mapping, structured violation JSON): none bears on a time bound.
Keyboard navigation of the CLI and the TUI's focus, mouse and resize sequences: the chunk changes no key or terminal-event handling.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (the MCP tools' contract as landed) — set MCP `wait`'s `timeout_ms` to `min(given, 50 000)` (`WAIT_CAP`, `wait_timeout`, 50 000 by default) because claude 2.1.287's stdio tool-call default was measured live only as "exceeds 50 s", the exact default unmeasured. It also recorded under [Delivery Confirmation] that the client timeout sits above the 18.5 s send total, and set `invalid-params` / `-32603` and `ttlMs` 0 / `cacheScope` `private` on `tools/list`. This is the standing ground the chunk re-measures: `decision/mcp-wait-cap` and `decision/send-time-bound` rest on a reading that gave no exact number, and a new cap or bound replaces or tightens it.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (MCP list builds the board and reads agents; the Tokio client; the plugin registers viola mcp) — MCP `list` runs `list::board_document` on a blocking thread and makes one `claude agents --json` read per call, a ratified widening. The Tokio flavour sits in `viola-channel`'s feature-gated `TokioClient`. Only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), with rmcp release features exactly `server` + `transport-io` (`scripts/rmcp-features.sh`), and `viola-e2e` takes rmcp `client` alone. `.mcp.json` registers `viola mcp`, and `mcp.ndjson` gets its lines. Trap: a tokio timeout bound in `viola-mcp` (for example tokio's `time` feature) is a dependency/feature change under `decision/tokio-only-in-mcp-crate`, `sync-core-tokio-only-in-mcp` and the channel tree-form ban. List's longest block is the board read plus the agents read.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — added `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` = 40 s (PROVISIONAL) beside the 10 s window, through `SendSlot::window()`. It stated that a compact send's blocking total "gains 48.5 s plus the paste, under the MCP tool-call ceiling read at 50 012 ms". This is `send`'s known longest block and the one figure nearest the client bound: a 48.5 s+paste path under a ~50 s reading leaves almost no margin, so it is the first gap the chunk must close or prove (`decision/compact-confirm-window`).

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — raised `GATE_MAX_WAIT` to 8.5 s, the founder's ruling to cover the CLI's 8.0 s paste hint. It set `send`'s block to "at most 18.5 s (8.5 s and 10 s)" and added the second wheel/turn read after the gate. This is the origin of the `send-time-bound` figure. Trap it recorded: a case reading a verified, literal-less screen through a clock that never advances waits forever. A bound test must drive a real or advancing clock.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** (the paste hint measured on the live CLI, and the founder's decision) — the founder chose the 8.5 s wait on a priced card that named `send`'s longest block as 18.5 s. This is the precedent that raising a bound on `send` is priced and ruled by the founder, not by a delegate.

**2026-10-04-readiness-gate-and-timing-constants** — named the timing constants (`QUIET_PERIOD`, `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK`) as compiled PROVISIONAL built-ins. It made `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` = 1 s the product bound and kept the hook's 750 ms `CONNECT_DEADLINE` asserted below it. This is the precedent for the "compiled bound with a test" branch: a constant held below another bound by a unit assertion (`decision/hook-connect-deadline`, `decision/spine-deadline`).

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** — made `quiet-period` and `confirm-window` ledger rows validate the compiled timing constants per CLI version, with run reading no number from the stamp. This is the precedent for the "relied ledger row with a verify probe" branch of the chunk's fork: a timing value stays compiled and a per-version row validates it (`decision/confirm-window-compiled`, `gate-timings-compiled`).

**2026-10-04-wait-and-last** — built `wait {after?, timeout_ms?, from?}` with `u64` params (else `-32602`), a `checked_add` deadline, and the `WaitFeed` Condvar wake with no file polling. It also built `last`. `wait`'s caller-supplied block is this deadline, so any cap stays inside the u64 / `-32602` contract (`contract/channel-wait/params`, `channel-wait/timeout-ms`).

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — moved the hold to `dialog_hold_s` (60–3600 s). It bounded the hook's reply read at `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s`, with the `hooks.json` timeout 3615 s set above it so that viola, never Claude Code, ends the wait. It also added `dialog-expired` as a wake kind. This is the precedent for keeping viola's own bound below the host's timeout by a pinned margin (`decision/viola-ends-the-dialog-wait`). A parked MCP `wait` can span a hold, so it must stay capped.

**2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes** — made `send` consume `LOCAL_COMMANDS`. An unconfirmable command returns at once with no window, and `/clear` on a verified CLI waits the window for its post-condition. These are the per-command branches of `send`'s block that the bound must cover.

**2026-11-16-local-command-delivery** — added stdout-echo confirmation (a transcript tag count, the read bounded by MAX_FRAME) and the `unconfirmable` case for an unreadable transcript, ratified 2026-11-17. This adds another confirmation path whose wait is part of `send`'s longest block (`decision/local-command-echo-confirmation`, `contract/send-results/unconfirmable`).

**2026-11-19-context-as-a-local-command** — added the `/context` local command with its own relied row and Run B's eighth paste, and extended `unconfirmable` to any listed command on an unverified CLI. This is one more listed command whose window and post-condition feed the send total. It is also the most recent precedent for a widening of verify's pastes, held PROVISIONAL for the epoch batch.

**2026-11-16-send-confirmation** — put `send`'s post-gate section (second wheel/turn read, link, `send-issued`, paste) under one wrapper flight lock that the claim and turn/wheel moves also take, and widened the prompt match to the submitted form. Lock waits add to `send`'s whole path (`decision/send-flight-lock`, `submitted-form-prompt-match`).

**2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records** — built the confirmed `send`: the `send-issued` / `send-confirmed` / `send-refused` records, the refusal order, one send in flight (`turn-running`), and a paste failing after issue answered `input-not-ready`. A compiled bound or split that ends a send early must keep these records and the refusal order (`contract/send-refusal/order`, `contract/send/paste-failure-after-issue`).

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — removed the `budget-paused` rung from `send`'s refusal order, and retired exit 11 never to be reused (`decision/retired-exit-codes-never-reused`). If the chunk adds a timeout outcome, it may not reuse 11. The refusal-order rows it touches are the ones it last rewrote.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** — added the server identity check (peer pid and start time) to every frame client, the MCP frame tools included. In MCP the start time is read on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. The MCP result is `instance-unreachable` with no frame and no line. These client-side checks are the first part of `send`'s and `wait`'s whole path on the MCP surface (`decision/frame-client-verifies-server`, `server-start-time-read-through-sysinfo`).

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the instance check first at every CLI frame verb and MCP frame tool) — made each MCP frame tool run `check_instance` before `live_endpoint`, a refusal giving `instance-unreachable` with no frame and no line. It also moved snapshot readers onto the replay. This fixes the order of the MCP frame path a bound must wrap (`decision/frame-client-check-order`, `mcp-frame-tools-strict-modes-check`).

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** — added the socket-directory check and the peer euid check to every client, the MCP `frame` among them (`socket-dir-refused`, `server-verify-failed`). It set the check order: strict-modes, liveness, socket dir, euid, then pid. These are the last client-side checks before `send`'s frame on MCP.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — set exit 21 / MCP `instance-unreachable`'s closed cause set and `result::unreachable(cause)`. It read `Closed | Io` as `endpoint-lost`, and the founder ratified the cause crossing to drivers. Any new outcome for a call cut at a bound must fit or extend a closed set through `viola-core`, with the founder's word on a crossing (`contract/unreachable-cause/cause-set`, `decision/mcp-unreachable-result-for-every-cause`).

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — made MCP error results carry codes and fixed messages only, held by the census `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`. It set `wrapper-fault` through `sanitised_fault`, and `viola mcp` now exits 1 on a stdin cut before `initialize`. A new MCP timeout or split result must be a named row of that census (`decision/sanitised-error-surfaces`).

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — capped `viola mcp`'s stdin with `CappedLines` at MAX_FRAME, handed to rmcp 3.4.1 (whose stdio `read_until` is unbounded), and added the bounded-readers census `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs`. This is the precedent for bounding inside the reader viola hands rmcp rather than patching rmcp. Any new reader the chunk adds must be bounded or named (`decision/bounded-readers`).

**2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii** (the recorded live MCP exchange: the tap; the measured 2.1.302 MCP opening) — added the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (`record` / `fixture`) and the `Mcp.<variant>.json` class with its schema, recorded live on two founder-capped starts. It measured that 2.1.302 opens with `server/discover` and no `initialize`. This is the precedent and instrument for reading the CLI's MCP client side. Recording it again is a ratified boundary crossing, and this phase makes no live start.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — bounded the `claude agents --json` read (`run::agents::read_logged`: `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, a 5 s kill) that MCP `list` makes on each call, failing to the `unknown` statuses. This sets `list`'s longest block, which must sit below the client bound (`decision/agents-listing-never-errors`, `mcp-list-reads-agents`).

**2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings** — measured that a session with both plugins starts the `--plugin-dir` plugin's `viola mcp`, and that an exit-1 `viola mcp` does not block the CLI's start. This tells which server's tool calls the client bound applies to.

body: The viola mcp tool set (send, wait, last, answer, list): each tool's longest block is bounded in code, and that bound sits below the client's tool-call timeout.

The send tool's whole path is bounded end to end: the client-side checks before any request (empty text, control character), the frame, the wrapper's wheel read, the typing and the delivery confirmation with its waits.

The wait tool's caller-supplied wait: capped or bounded so the whole call ends below the client's bound; its outcomes (turn-ended, dialog, dialog-expired, timed out) stay the ones the wait verb already reports, and turn-ended stays no send outcome.
The last, answer and list tools: each one's longest block is read and bounded, the same as send and wait.
A call that reaches its bound, or an argument over its cap, returns through the existing tool result shapes (refusal or invalid-params), never a new shape and never a silent hang.
The CLI send and wait path the MCP tools share through the channel crate's Tokio client: the deadlines its calls carry, and who waits on what, are what the bound is measured against.
The wrapper's send handling (wheel read, typing, delivery confirmation and its waits): its time bounds are counted inside the send tool's bound.

The client's MCP tool-call timeout for the versions viola stamps (2.1.328, and 2.1.330 as the bare claude on the host): its default, the names that move it (names only), whether a stdio server differs, whether progress notifications reset it, and what happens at the bound (the error class; the call alone or the server torn down).
That timeout is read from strings of the installed bundles only: a READING, not a measurement; no live start, and nothing of the operator's real claude home is read.
Each gap closed (a compiled bound, a cap on a caller's argument, or a documented split) carries a test that can fail when the bound is breached.

How the bound stands is a fork priced at P3: a relied capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe (a 30th row beside the 29), or a compiled bound with a test and a drift reading; the ledger's rows, verify's child set and the residual rows are reached only on the first branch.
Whatever viola verify or a rig would newly read, write or spawn is a widening said whole at P3, with what is kept and where, and a proof that no text reaches a file, stamp, fixture or log.
The MCP server keeps no human surface and keeps hiding the wheel and handoff verbs: bounding the tools adds no tool and no human output.
No documentation leaf gains a figure the code states: a bound's value lives in the code, not in prose.
The pinned product build stays untouched; the product re-pin stays outside this chunk.
